extracted.intended_audience: aspiring book reviewers; readers wanting to learn how to write book reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step guidance for composing an online or print book review that summarizes the book without spoilers, evaluates its strengths and weaknesses objectively, and gives a clear recommendation and audience guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Reveal the genre, theme, main conflict, and main characters in the story — without giving away spoilers or revealing how the story ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good rule of thumb is not to mention anything that happens beyond the midpoint. Set the stage and give readers a sense of the book without explaining how the central issue is resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction summary: provide context and authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-fiction, the primary goal of the summary is to provide context: what problems or issues the book spots and how it addresses them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be sure to mention the authors of the title and what experience or expertise they bring to the title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present an evaluation that mixes subjective and objective critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Weave your personal take into the review but don’t base the evaluation only on subjective opinion; also objectively critique stronger and weaker elements and provide examples from the text to back up your points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record your reactions and thoughts as you read. Describe how the story affected you and then identify specific strengths and weaknesses with supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Back up claims with textual examples
rubrics_metrics.description: When you say the prose is evocative or a character is unbelievable, show readers by providing an actual (non-spoiler) passage or referencing a scene that displays the point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quotations or concrete scene references to demonstrate both positive and negative assessments rather than asserting opinions without support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate prose and authorial style
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the author’s style, sentence structure, dialogue, descriptive prose, and how these contribute to the reading experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss elements like short punchy sentences, deadpan humour, descriptive prose, or other stylistic choices and how they serve the story (examples in the page cite how style animates characters and events).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparisons to other books or authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw comparisons to well-known titles or authors to give readers a quick sense of tone, pacing, or genre expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state likenesses (e.g., ’reminiscent of Agatha Christie’) to help situate the book for potential readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge reader taste and specific story elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that enjoyment depends on individual preferences and call out particular elements that will divide readers (e.g., piecemeal worldbuilding, an enigmatic magic system).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain who might like or dislike those choices and give concrete examples from the book showing how those elements function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction evaluation: judge clarity and effectiveness of arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-fiction, evaluate how clearly and effectively the book communicates its points and supports its arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address key takeaways, readability, and whether the evidence or reasoning convincingly supports the book’s claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give a clear recommendation and target audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclude by indicating whether you would recommend the book and specify what kinds of readers will enjoy it (or won’t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You don’t have to write the words ‘I recommend this book’—you can make the recommendation clear through highlighted favorable opinion or by naming fan-audiences (e.g., ‘fans of so-and-so will enjoy this book’).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance negative reviews by noting positives
rubrics_metrics.description: If you don’t recommend the book, still share enjoyable elements before explaining why you wouldn’t recommend it overall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State what worked (e.g., certain scenes, concepts, or moments) and then explain the reasons for the lower overall judgement (e.g., unsophisticated vocabulary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction recommendation: disclose prior expectations and bias
rubrics_metrics.description: When recommending or not, for non-fiction reviewers should state their prior expectations or biases because those affect receptivity to the book’s arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain your perspective going in (e.g., professional background or ideological stance) so readers can gauge how your bias shaped your evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have an opinion and make it clear from the outset
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should have a stance — positive, negative, or mixed — and make it evident early in the review, not buried until the conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weave your opinion into the summary so readers know your overall take from the start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide bibliographic and contextual details
rubrics_metrics.description: Include useful book facts: is it a debut? Part of a series? Author’s prior books and background? Page count? Publisher? Price?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weave this information into the review so readers have the practical and contextual details they need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow publication-specific guidelines and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapt content and tone depending on where you’re publishing the review (Goodreads vs. The New York Times, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check and follow the target outlet’s guidelines for length, tone, spoilers, and acceptable content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record reactions and notes while reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep notes of your reactions as you read to help craft a thorough and specific evaluation later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jot down passages, lines, and scenes that surprised or moved you so you can reference them when writing the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn by reading other reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Study published reviews to see examples of summaries, evaluations, and recommendations and to learn different critical approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use other reviewers’ examples (the site links many sample reviews) as models for structure, tone, and evidence use.
